newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil current account gap still seen growing-CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil current account gap still seen growing-CNI.

text.p: Recent measures taken by the Brazilian government to plug its current account balance of payments gap are insufficient to reverse the expansion in the deficit but should slow its growth, the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.

"The batch of measures adopted by the government to reduce the imbalance in the current account and to make it easier to finance are not in themselves capable of producing a significant change in the country's external accounts," the CNI said.

"Nevertheless, aided by a slowdown in economic growth, the measures ought to be able to reduce the likelihood of further deterioration in the external accounts," it added in a preview of a report due to be published on Tuesday.

Faced with an expanding current account gap, which reached 3.9 percent of gross domestic product in the 12 months to April compared with 3.25 percent for 1996, the government recently took a number of steps to boost exports and stem imports.
It raised the tax on credit operations to stiffle domestic demand for some imported goods, especially household appliances, and banned the financing of credit card purchases abroad.

In addition, it has tried to keep Brazil attractive to foreign capital, for instance opening up the derivatives market to hedging operations involving foreigners and slowing down the pace of interest rate declines.
